about.purpose: Plan for the Design Release 2.1 business review page: one card per change a user would notice, the open questions to put first, and the screenshots to capture. Built from the 40 rows marked done across journey-foundation, reference-lists, commodities-and-reason, arrival-and-transit, origin-page and overview-and-review. The templates theme is not in yet.
about.capture: Same data, same viewport (desktop 1280 wide, full page), JavaScript on unless a shot says otherwise. Each shot is taken once on a main stack and once on a combined-branch stack, unless compare is 'after-only'. Where a shot is about a browser title, a dropdown's options or what a screen reader hears, alsoCapture says what to record beside the picture.

routes.live animals: List /live-animals. Create: the create button on the list POSTs /live-animals/notifications and opens /live-animals/notifications/{id}/origin. Overview /live-animals/notifications/{id}. Pages /live-animals/notifications/{id}/{slug}: origin, commodities (What are you importing?), import-reason, consignment-details (Commodity details), commodities/identification, additional-details, port-of-entry (Arrival details), transit-countries, transporters, accompanying-documents (Upload documents), addresses (Roles and addresses), cph-number, consignment/contact/select (Contact address), notification-view (review, draft review and submitted view share this route), declaration, confirmation, cancel-amend, delete. Amend is a POST to .../amend from the list row's Amend action or the view's 'Amend this notification'.
routes.plants: List /high-risk-plants. Create: the start button POSTs and opens /high-risk-plants/notifications/{id}/commodity-type. Overview /high-risk-plants/notifications/{id}. Opening run: commodity-type, commodities/details, commodities, origin, arrival-status (not for potatoes), arrival-details, destinations/select, consignors/select, identification-numbers, consignment/contact/select, notification-view (check your answers), declaration, confirmation.

openQuestions.title: Is the new order of the first run right?
openQuestions.question: Is this the right order for a trader filling in a new notification? In particular: should the CPH number stop being a step in the first run, so a trader who needs one has to notice its row on roles and addresses? And should the run end on the review page, listing what is missing, rather than on the overview?
openQuestions.asBuilt: Live animals: origin, what are you importing, main import reason, commodity details, identification details (only if the animals need it), additional details, arrival details, transit countries (rail or road only), transport details, upload documents, roles and addresses, contact address, then the review. The CPH number page is never shown in the run and opens only from its row on roles and addresses. If every overview task is already complete, roles and addresses goes to the overview. The contact address always goes to the review, even when unfinished; the review of a draft is now headed by the reference with a Draft tag (not 'Review your notification') and its Back link goes to the notification list, not the overview. Plants keeps its own order, but its last step (consignment contact) now goes to check your answers even when unfinished, and Continue there shows the missing answers instead of going to the overview.

openQuestions.title: Is it right to let traders leave a page half-done, but stop them when one answer is in the wrong format?
openQuestions.question: Should 'Save and return to overview' save a half-finished page? And when one answer is in the wrong format, is it right that the whole page is refused, so the trader's other answers on that page are not saved either? Should commodity details and the contact address keep insisting on their answers?
openQuestions.asBuilt: On origin, what are you importing, main import reason, identification details, additional details, arrival details, transit countries, transport details, upload documents and roles and addresses, 'Save and return to overview' saves whatever was entered with no error and the task does not show Complete. An answer that breaks its own format rule (for example an arrival date of 31/2/2027, a malformed region code, an exit date of 31/2/2026) is refused with its error and nothing on the page is saved. Commodity details and the contact address still show their errors and save nothing. Plants behaves the same, refusing a date that is not real, a future date once arrived, a time not on the 24-hour clock, a port not on the list or a quantity that is not a whole number. This overlaps EUDPA-667's mandatory-to-submit work.

openQuestions.title: Are the amend buttons right, and what should Continue do on an unfinished amendment?
openQuestions.question: Are three ways off each page (back to the amend review, on to the next page, or to the overview) right for a trader making an amendment? And when a trader presses Continue on an unfinished amendment, should the page stay put silently, as Design Release 2.1 draws it, or show an error summary naming what is missing, as built? The row asked for the silent hold; the review-page row asked for the error summary; the build followed the second.
openQuestions.asBuilt: While amending, each page the overview links to ends with 'Save and return' (primary, to the amend review), 'Save and continue' (secondary, to the next page) and a link-styled 'Save and return to overview', with no cancel link. The address pickers, the CPH number page, the permanent address page and the contact address page show only the first two. Back links stay as in the journey and never go to the amend review. Continue on an unfinished amend review does not submit: the review is shown again with 'There is a problem' and, for example, 'Complete arrival details' (tests repo amend-endings.spec.ts:113-131). It opens with no errors showing. Plants: the same three controls, its pickers two buttons, and the same refusal on Continue.

openQuestions.title: Does asking the reason between the two commodity pages read right?
openQuestions.question: Walking from origin to arrival details, does it make sense to a trader to choose the animals, then give the import reason, then say how many animals there are? Are the Back links on both commodity pages right?
openQuestions.asBuilt: The commodity page's Back goes to origin; its Save and continue goes to main import reason. Commodity details now comes after main import reason, and its Back goes to the commodity page. From commodity details, Save and continue goes to identification details when any chosen species needs identifiers, otherwise to additional details when it applies, otherwise to arrival details. Opened from the overview each page returns to the overview; opened from the review it returns to the review. Both pages keep 'Save and return to overview' and 'Cancel and return to overview'. The performance tests walk the same order.

openQuestions.title: Is the order right for cattle and for horses only, and are both Back links right?

Should Back on main import reason go to what are you importing, and Back on additional details go to the page before it?
openQuestions.asBuilt: In the first run, main import reason's Back goes to what are you importing and its Save and continue goes to commodity details. Additional details is reached from identification details when a chosen species needs identifiers, otherwise from commodity details, never straight from main import reason; its Back mirrors that, and its Save and continue goes to arrival details. Opened from the overview, both pages have Back to the overview and return there on save. The tests walk cattle by air and a horse by sea (temporary admission) in this order.

openQuestions.title: Is the flatter review page, with renamed cards, right?
openQuestions.question: Is it right to remove the heading above each card on the review, so cards sit straight under the numbered sections, and to rename the sections and cards? Do 'Origin of import', 'Main import reason', '4. Uploaded documents', '5. Consignment addresses' with one 'Addresses' card, and '6. Contact address' read right to traders?
openQuestions.asBuilt: No heading sits between a numbered section and its cards ('Where is this consignment coming from?', 'Main reason for import', 'Upload documents', 'Roles and addresses' and 'Contact address for this consignment' are gone as headings), and card titles moved up one heading level. Section 4 is '4. Uploaded documents' and section 5 '5. Consignment addresses' with a single 'Addresses' card whose Change link opens roles and addresses. Unfinished messages follow the new names: 'Complete origin of import', 'Complete main import reason', 'Complete additional details'.

openQuestions.title: Is the commodity card layout right, and where should its Change links go?
openQuestions.question: Is one card per commodity with a block per species clear? Is it right to have two Change links to the same page on one card: one at the top of the card and one on each species' first row? And should Latin species names be capitalised word by word ('Bos Taurus'), as the prototype shows, when the scientific convention is 'Bos taurus'?
openQuestions.asBuilt: Section 1 has a 'What are you importing?' card (commodity code, common name, species, each listed once). Section 2 has one card per commodity titled '<name> (<code>)', with a block per species headed by its title-cased Latin name, showing 'Number of animals', 'Number of packages (when required)' where packaging applies, and an 'Identification details' table. The card's top Change link and the 'Number of animals' row's Change link both open commodity details; the identification table has its own Change link to the identification page (species-block.js:36-68). Species error messages use the lower-case name, for example 'Enter at least 1 animal identifier for bos taurus'.

openQuestions.asBuilt: The submitted view, the draft review and the amend review share one page address (notification-view). The page decides by the notification's stored status: Submitted or Submitted action required gives a read-only view headed by the reference (also the browser title), a status tag, 'Date submitted: <d Month yyyy>', no status strip, Amend this notification, Copy as new and Delete at the top, and the Import reference numbers section. A Draft gets the same header with a Draft tag and 'Date created', and stays editable. An amendment keeps 'Review your notification' with the status strip. Back on the submitted view and the draft review goes to the set's own list (/live-animals or /high-risk-plants); the INS home also links here, so Back from there lands on the live animals list, not the INS home. An unknown notification goes to the list.

openQuestions.asBuilt: One row asked for the strip's Cancel amend on the review as well; another asked for a Cancel amend button at the foot instead of the old link. As built, the amend review's strip shows the Amend tag and reference with no Cancel amend (check-answers/controller.js:155-157, offerCancelAmend: false), and the foot has Continue, Cancel amend and Delete.

openQuestions.title: Should a draft show import reference numbers and put Delete at the top?
openQuestions.question: A draft's review now shows 'Import reference numbers' with the warning 'You must use the correct reference and code on the customs declaration or your consignment will be delayed.' before the notification is submitted. Is that right for a draft? And is Delete at the top of the page, rather than beside Continue at the foot, where traders expect it?
openQuestions.asBuilt: Draft review: reference heading, Draft tag, 'Date created', Copy as new and a red Delete at the top, the Import reference numbers section with the reference and C640, then the editable cards and errors, ending with Continue only. The review-ending row had put Delete beside Continue; the later draft-header row moved it to the top (check-answers/template.njk:41-81 and 145-165). Plants' draft check your answers has its delete button in the header and no Copy as new.

openQuestions.title: The INS home shows the new status as a code
openQuestions.question: The INS home's notification table shows each status exactly as stored, so a notification needing action reads 'SUBMITTED_ACTION_REQUIRED'. Should the table show 'Submitted action required', or wait for the INS dashboard rework?
openQuestions.asBuilt: repos/trade-imports-ins-frontend/src/server/app/features/dashboard/controller.js:54 puts notification.status into the table as text (unchanged from main, where it already shows 'SUBMITTED' and 'DRAFT'). The build only changed where the row links (view-model/list.js:89-100). The INS dashboard's summary rework is blocked until its requirements firm up.

openQuestions.title: Two plants gaps left by this release
openQuestions.question: What is the customs document code for a plants notification, so it can be added to plants' Import reference numbers? And is it acceptable that plants' amend review never changes its heading to 'Review before re-submitting', until plants' backend can say whether answers changed?
openQuestions.asBuilt: Plants' Import reference numbers shows the notification reference only (C640 is the animals code). Plants' amend review keeps its heading whatever changes. The afternoon ruling (claim 51) says this heading is recorded in deferred.md for plants to follow later, but deferred.md has no entry for it yet.

openQuestions.title: Port of exit offers every port, not only those approved for animals
openQuestions.question: Is it acceptable for now that both port of exit dropdowns offer every port, including ones not approved for animals, because the master data has no flag to filter on?
openQuestions.asBuilt: Transit and temporary admission port of exit dropdowns list every port reference data serves, airports then seaports then rail. deferred.md records a ticket under EUDPA-190 if MDM ever adds the flag.

openQuestions.title: Traders will see MDM's duplicate and misspelt ports
openQuestions.question: The port lists show master data as it is, including duplicate Pembroke and Sheerness ports and names such as 'Teestort', 'TILBURY' and 'Portsmouth  Port'. Has the MDM team been told, and is it acceptable to show them until MDM corrects them?
openQuestions.asBuilt: Lists are never edited in code. deferred.md: Slack message to the MDM team drafted 9 October, for Sam to send.

openQuestions.title: New Welsh text is machine-drafted
openQuestions.question: Who will review the Welsh for the changed commodity page and commodity details wording before release?
openQuestions.asBuilt: Every English string the commodity row changed or added has a Welsh counterpart marked as a machine draft for translator review. Other rows added Welsh for their changes (main import reason, origin hints, Amend and Cancel amend), but the rows do not say whether a translator has checked them.

openQuestions.title: Some country lists search as you type, others are plain dropdowns
openQuestions.question: Is it acceptable for this release that country of origin and transit countries search as you type, but the transhipment destination country, port of exit and the INS address book country stay plain dropdowns of about 250 entries?
openQuestions.asBuilt: Rolling the search component out is EUDPA-635's work. deferred.md lists a follow-on ticket (not raised) for the transhipment destination country, the animals address country and the INS address book country.

openQuestions.title: Parts of these pages wait on design
openQuestions.question: Design needs to answer before these are built: the Search button beside the country and port boxes, the live region code prefix, custom screen reader announcements on the country search, and the Copy buttons on Import reference numbers. Are the pages acceptable without them?
openQuestions.asBuilt: Each is its own blocked increment in the waiting-on-design theme (afternoon ruling claims 8 to 22). The 12 design questions in js-triage/triage-2026-10-09.md are still to be sent to design (deferred.md).
